summary: Gorontalo stands under Indonesia's national framework. The source inventory records no ordinance, raid, protection measure, facility or support service specific to Gorontalo in either direction, so the national assessment applies.
tangentialFactors:
Vigilante violence against transgender people is documented nationally: a wave of attacks on 14-16 July 2026 saw mobs attack trans women across the country, including more than 15 trans women in Bogor who were doused, stripped and beaten, with footage circulated online. A researcher cited in the reporting documents markedly hardened anti-queer attitudes since 2016.

An October 2025 presidential decree lists "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among nonmilitary threats alongside terrorism, radicalism and drug addiction, placing LGBTQ+ people inside national security policy. Provincial moral laws and Aceh's caning regime remain in force.

Indonesia does not criminalise same-sex activity in private, but provides no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection. The 2022 penal-code amendment criminalising sex outside marriage took effect on 2 January 2026 and carries up to one year in prison; because same-sex marriage is not permitted, that provision reaches consensual same-sex relations.

Legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery and judicial approval, and Indonesia recognises only male and female sex descriptors. A 2025 Pew survey found 93% of Indonesians rate homosexuality "morally unacceptable," and Indonesia voted against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity in 2016, 2022 and 2025.

outOfScopeNotes:
